reader.requirement: At --std 85 OPEN EXTEND of a relative file (sequential access only, a level-2 form of this edition) positions after the currently existing record with the highest relative record number, so the next WRITE releases highest+1 (1 for an empty or newly created optional file) and returns it in the RELATIVE KEY item.

edition-consulted.switches: OPEN's implementor-default sharing mode (ALL OTHER at 85)
DialectBehavior.RelativeWriteKeyOutOfRangeIsPermanentError, random/dynamic arm only (not reached by a sequential EXTEND release)

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectBehaviors over KeyedConnector.cs, RelativeConnector.cs; NextSequentialSlot reads the tree's last key at each release with no edition; CheckOpenModeForFile's EXTEND/access check has no edition test
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf21_04; this probe adds EXTEND after the highest record was deleted, EXTEND over an emptied file, EXTEND of an absent OPTIONAL file, a non-optional absent file, varying-length records, and the EXTEND-on-dynamic refusal

reader.notes: The positioning is NextSequentialSlot's live read of the tree's last key (max with the connector's last release), so a deleted top record lowers the next number correctly. Side observation, outside this rule: COBOL2372 at --std 85 cites §2023:14.9.27.3 SR2 rather than §1985:VIII.4.4.3 SR1 (a citation-text issue in StatementValidation#CheckOpenModeForFile, not a behaviour defect).

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-132/rext.cob (rext-003): file written by random access at 2,7,9, record 9 deleted; OPEN EXTEND (sequential, RELATIVE KEY SK) releases 8 then 9 (SE1=00 0008, SE2=00 0009); OPEN EXTEND of a file with no RELATIVE KEY clause (third SELECT over the same file) releases 10; EXTEND then READ is 47 and the next WRITE releases 11; INPUT listing 2,7,8,9,10,11 then AT END. rextr.cob: OPEN EXTEND of a RANDOM access relative file refused at compile (COBOL2372; the reader showed DYNAMIC).
